title: North Korea's missile month, and the price of a Trump meeting
deck: Three weapons launches in twelve days, ending with the first reported submarine-fired cruise missiles since January 2024, look like Pyongyang raising the price of a Kim-Trump meeting that Trump says he 'may' hold in November.
region: North Korea, Korean Peninsula, Northeast Asia

card.headline: Kim is testing weapons while Trump dangles a meeting, which raises the price of talks

keyNumber.label: launch events in 12 days (3, 12 and 14 October), the latest from a submarine

forYou.line: Expect short-lived market jitters on launch days. Expect no direct supply disruption unless a launch lands near shipping or air lanes.
Past Korean Peninsula tests have mostly produced brief moves in the Korean won and stocks. Treat that as a pattern, not a rule.
The sub-launched cruise missile test is the new element. Watch whether more follow before Trump's November Asia trip.
The bigger question is diplomatic. A Trump-Kim meeting is possible but unconfirmed, and Pyongyang appears to be bargaining first.

effects.text: North Korea fires two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast on 14 October, including a Pulhwasal-3-31
The launch follows a hypersonic intermediate-range missile on 3 October and two ballistic missiles on 12 October that flew more than 560 miles
Seoul, Washington and Tokyo face another round of condemnation and consultation, with the tests landing close to a DMZ landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers
Pyongyang raises its price for talks just as Trump says he 'may' meet Kim during his November Asia trip
South Korea and North Korea trade weapons milestones, as Seoul carried out its first hypersonic test days before the 12 October launches
Pressure grows on allies to show readiness without wrecking the chance of summitry
Submarine-fired missiles are harder to detect before launch than land-based ones, which complicates early warning for South Korea, Japan and US forces
The China-hosted APEC meeting in Shenzhen on 18-19 November gains a second agenda item, with Kim looming over Trump's Xi diplomacy
Any Trump-Putin-Xi summit on Ukraine would change Kim's leverage, given Pyongyang's troops-for-technology alliance with Moscow
US credibility is tested at the same time in Northeast Asia and the South China Sea, where Philippine-Chinese clashes spiked in early October

whatHappened: On 14 October, North Korea fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast, according to state media. One was a Pulhwasal-3-31. It was the first reported sub-launched cruise missile test since January 2024.

The test capped a busy month. On 3 October the North fired a hypersonic intermediate-range missile. On 12 October it fired two ballistic missiles that flew more than 560 miles. That was days after South Korea's first hypersonic test and a landmine blast on the DMZ that wounded three South Korean soldiers.
On 12 October, Trump said he 'may' meet Kim Jong Un during his November Asia trip. The 14 October launch came two days later.
whyItMatters: The pattern suggests bargaining through weapons. Testing while a meeting is on offer signals that Pyongyang wants to talk from a position of strength, not on Washington's terms. That reading is our judgement; North Korea has not said so.

Submarine launch is a capability step. Missiles fired from underwater are harder to track before launch, so they complicate defence planning for South Korea, Japan and US forces. We cannot judge from the reporting how far along the programme is.

The timing is awkward for Washington. Trump is due at the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, hosted by Xi, following Xi's September state visit to Washington. Beijing controls that agenda, and Kim's tests give China and Russia more to trade on.

winners.why: It shows capability and keeps the initiative while a US president is publicly open to a meeting, at the cost of only condemnation so far.
A distracted, stretched US leaves both with more room, and North Korea's alliance with Moscow adds to Russia's leverage over any wider settlement. This is analysis, not a reported fact.

winners.who: Defence contractors and missile-defence planners in the US, South Korea and Japan
winners.why: Another demonstration of sub-launched and hypersonic threats strengthens the case for early-warning and interception spending.

losers.why: It has to deal with testing from the North, a DMZ mine incident that wounded three of its soldiers, and an arms race that its own hypersonic test has fed.
Missiles flying toward its waters or sea lanes leave it the most exposed to surprise, and it has little say in whether Trump meets Kim.
Each test makes a nuclear-limits agreement look further away, and raises the political cost to Trump of meeting Kim without concessions.

whatsNext: More launches are plausible before the November trip. The October tempo suggests Pyongyang wants to be seen as negotiating from strength.
18-19 November: APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen. Whether a Trump-Kim meeting is announced will be the key signal.
Watch Washington's tone and whether Seoul and Tokyo are consulted before any meeting is offered.
Any Trump-Putin-Xi summit on Ukraine would feed back into Kim's leverage.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what is the most likely path between now and the end of the Asia trip?
options: Tests stop and a Trump-Kim meeting is announced
More tests, no meeting, with diplomacy kept open
A major escalation such as a nuclear test
Quiet, with no more tests and no news
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 45%, is calibrated pressure: more launches or provocations, no meeting, and both sides keeping the door open. A summit pivot is judged at about 20%.

recap.question: What was new about the 14 October test?
options: It was a submarine-launched cruise missile test, the first reported since January 2024
It was an intercontinental ballistic missile

recap.question: What did Trump say on 12 October?
options: He may meet Kim during his November Asia trip

recap.question: Where is the APEC leaders' meeting on 18-19 November?

timeline.title: Xi's state visit to Washington ends
timeline.detail: It ended with a declared 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' but few concrete trade deliverables, setting up the November Shenzhen meeting.

timeline.title: North Korea fires a hypersonic intermediate-range missile
timeline.detail: The first of three launch events in twelve days, as reported in coverage of the October launches.

timeline.title: Two ballistic missiles fly more than 560 miles
timeline.detail: This came days after South Korea's first hypersonic test and a DMZ landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers. The same day, Trump said he 'may' meet Kim on his November Asia trip.

timeline.title: Submarine-launched cruise missiles fired off the east coast
timeline.detail: Two types of strategic cruise missile, including a Pulhwasal-3-31, the first reported sub-launched cruise test since January 2024.

timeline.title: State media and wire services report the test
timeline.detail: Al Jazeera and Stars and Stripes carry the story under the framing of mounting October launches.

causes.name: Weapons development
causes.detail: North Korea has pursued sea-based and cruise missile capabilities for years; the Pulhwasal-3-31 type was previously reported tested in January 2024.

causes.name: Russia alliance
causes.detail: Pyongyang's troops-for-technology relationship with Moscow reduces its need for US or Chinese concessions.

causes.name: Alliance dilemma
causes.detail: Seoul, Tokyo and Washington must deter without closing the door on diplomacy.

causes.name: Trump's offer
causes.detail: Trump said on 12 October he 'may' meet Kim on the November trip. Pyongyang appears to be signalling the price of such a meeting.

causes.name: South Korean hypersonic test
causes.detail: Seoul's first hypersonic test came days before the 12 October launches and probably fed the North's sense of an arms race. That link is our inference.

causes.name: DMZ landmine blast
causes.detail: A blast wounded three South Korean soldiers, raising tension on the border.

causes.name: APEC in Shenzhen
causes.detail: Beijing hosts Trump on 18-19 November, creating a deadline and a stage for Korea diplomacy.

causes.name: Great-power summitry
causes.detail: Putin's call for a Ukraine summit with Trump and Xi could reshape the leverage of all of Kim's patrons.

stakeholders.name: Kim Jong Un
stakeholders.wants: Recognition as a nuclear power and sanctions relief on his terms
stakeholders.leverage: Missile tests, the Russia relationship, and Trump's public interest in a meeting
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep testing, avoid a firm commitment to talks, and wait for US concessions before any summit

stakeholders.name: Donald Trump
stakeholders.wants: A headline diplomatic result and an orderly Asia trip
stakeholders.leverage: Summit access, sanctions policy and alliance backing
stakeholders.likelyMove: Stay open to a meeting while pressing allies for calm; say little about the launches

stakeholders.name: South Korean government
stakeholders.role: US treaty ally, in a weapons race with the North
stakeholders.wants: Deterrence, a seat at any US-North Korea table, and calm on the DMZ
stakeholders.leverage: Its own hypersonic programme and its alliance with Washington
stakeholders.likelyMove: Condemn the launches, consult with Washington and Tokyo, and continue its defence build-up

stakeholders.name: Japan
stakeholders.role: US treaty ally, within range of North Korean missiles
stakeholders.wants: Early warning, a say in any deal, and no deal that ignores its security
stakeholders.leverage: Intelligence sharing and missile defence cooperation
stakeholders.likelyMove: Protest and consult, and press Washington not to trade away allied interests

stakeholders.name: Xi Jinping and China
stakeholders.role: APEC host and North Korea's largest neighbour
stakeholders.wants: Stability on its border and a stronger hand in US trade talks
stakeholders.leverage: The APEC agenda and its economic ties to Pyongyang
stakeholders.likelyMove: Call for restraint, avoid blame, and use the summit to press for tariff relief

stakeholders.name: Vladimir Putin and Russia
stakeholders.wants: Continued military support and a Ukraine settlement on its terms
stakeholders.leverage: Technology and diplomatic cover for North Korea
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep Kim close while courting a summit with Trump and Xi

sectors.why: Sea-launched and hypersonic tests strengthen the case for early-warning and interception spending in South Korea, Japan and the US.
Launches usually cause short dips that fade. A sharper reaction would signal real escalation. This rests on past patterns, not on the cited reporting.

sectors.sector: Shipping and aviation near Korea and Japan
sectors.why: Launch days can trigger warnings and rerouting, though the cited reporting describes no disruption.
The tests raise the price of talks and the profile of Korea at a summit meant to focus on China-US trade.
Closer Pyongyang-Moscow ties support arms and technology exchange, though the cited sources give no numbers.

dailyLife.item: Travel to and around South Korea
dailyLife.effect: Launches rarely change travel conditions. Check official advisories if tension on the DMZ or at sea rises.
Short-lived dips in Korean assets have followed past launches. A pension or index fund is unlikely to be affected unless the crisis escalates.
Expect more emergency messages and defence briefings in South Korea and Japan if the launches continue.

scenarios.name: Calibrated pressure
scenarios.looksLike: More launches or provocations, no meeting. Both Washington and Pyongyang keep talk of a meeting alive.
signposts: Trump repeats that he 'may' meet Kim
North Korean state media avoids insulting Trump
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Allied nerves are tested, markets shrug, and summit diplomacy dominates the APEC story.

scenarios.name: Door ajar
scenarios.looksLike: Working-level contacts or messages through intermediaries, with launches paused but no summit.
signposts: Quiet from North Korean state media
A pause in launches for several weeks
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Tension eases without a deal; allies stay uneasy about being left out.

scenarios.name: Summit pivot
scenarios.looksLike: A Trump-Kim meeting is announced or held around the Asia trip, with a pause in tests.
signposts: Seoul or Beijing offering to host or facilitate
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Headline diplomacy returns, though real nuclear limits remain unlikely. Allies press for consultation.

scenarios.name: Sharp escalation
scenarios.looksLike: A much larger test, a nuclear test, or a deadly clash on the DMZ or at sea.
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Summit prospects collapse, markets sell off, and the US, Japan and South Korea harden their posture.

predictions.text: North Korea will carry out at least one more missile launch before the APEC leaders' meeting opens. Probability about 0.65.
A Trump-Kim meeting will take place during or immediately around the Asia trip. Probability about 0.12.
North Korea will carry out a nuclear test. Probability about 0.04.
Both sides will publicly confirm some direct contact or an agreed envoy channel. Probability about 0.2.

actions: Keep contingency plans for Korean and Japanese sites, covering communications and staff safety.
Do not change supply routes for launches alone; reassess only on escalation signals such as a nuclear test or a lethal clash.
Track the APEC agenda in Shenzhen for trade and tariff news that matters more than the tests.
Treat launch-day moves as noise unless they persist for more than a few days.
Watch defence and missile-defence names for policy-driven demand, and avoid assuming a sustained rally.
Watch for signs of a Trump-Kim meeting, which could move Korean assets either way.
If you live or travel in South Korea or Japan, follow official alerts and know local shelter guidance.
Avoid reacting to market dips in pensions or index funds unless you need the money soon.
Consult Seoul and Tokyo before any announcement about a meeting with Kim.
Separate defence readiness from diplomacy: condemn launches, but keep a channel open.
Coordinate with Beijing ahead of Shenzhen on what it will and will not do to restrain Pyongyang.

analogues.event: Missile tests followed by the Singapore summit
analogues.whatFollowed: A year of intense tests and threats gave way to a Trump-Kim meeting in June 2018, with a vague commitment on denuclearisation and little follow-through.
Talks broke down over sanctions relief and nuclear disclosure; weapons testing later resumed.
A brief, symbolic encounter produced a promise of working talks that never made progress.
Condemnation from the US, Japan and South Korea and no change in the North's course.

watch.title: APEC leaders' meeting opens in Shenzhen
watch.why: The first sign of whether Kim features in Trump's meeting with Xi, or whether a Trump-Kim meeting is announced.

watch.title: Further North Korean launches
watch.why: The pace and type of tests will show whether Pyongyang is pressing for talks or preparing a bigger step.

watch.title: Statements by Pyongyang on Trump's offer
watch.why: A public acceptance, rejection or conditions would clarify the price for talks.

watch.title: Putin's proposed summit with Trump and Xi
watch.why: Any move toward a Ukraine settlement would change Kim's leverage.

watch.title: DMZ incidents
watch.why: Another landmine blast or shooting would raise escalation risk quickly.

evidence.method: Drafted from two listed news articles and the event summary and connection notes supplied with them, without opening full article text. The facts about launch dates, distances, the DMZ blast and Trump's remark come from the summary. Everything about intent, capability, market effects and probabilities is the drafter's estimate and is labelled as such. No chart is included because there is no real numeric series to plot.
